notes.title: AI behavior, Detection Meter, March/April Progress
notes.content:
Hey folks,

During March and April we've been working on:
[list]
[*]shooting
[*]picking up and moving bodies
[*]enemy AI
[/list]

[h1][b]Shooting[/b][/h1]

Despite how easy it might sound, these are the things we had to take care of:
[list]
[*]is it trace or projectile?
[*]how to make a big weapon not clip with the character model
[*]should the trace go from the actual muzzle or from the third person camera
[*]what about a camera shake for impact
[*]what about vfx (and why doesn't it work properly?)
[*]should you go into melee combat while having a gun when the enemy gets to close, and if yes - what happens to the gun
[/list]
etc

So far the technical side of the shooting works, what's left is to add hit reactions. Without them it's hard to understand if it's a hit or miss.

Early iterations:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/6a0326c115b21175f87e300381fa35d2dec6e6ee.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/787bfaa5a05df1f9346b1346a5197809e3603ec7.gif[/img]

Later iterations:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/64294b459645b9423fe2ddf28a6149869f346f35.gif[/img]



[h1][b]Picking up bodies[/b][/h1]

We did it. And then we decided to switch to a universal animation library for all the characters, and it broke the feature completely. So we'll have to do it again.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/f55b6fca61be0f1544141cfe73e078c759eab857.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/b587bbc5f417dcb5cd6428049ccc45ef5ed15a0d.gif[/img]

At early stages of development it looked hilarious.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/fc0fa157f89001477e0ca031798115da96070b82.gif[/img]



[h1][b]Enemy AI[/b][/h1]

One of the biggest systems we worked on so far is the AI re-make. 

We did have an AI module before via UE blackboards, that already had sight and sound detection. However, we encountered some inflexibility of the system (and bugs) that didn't allow us to implement a more complex AI behavior. 

So we switched to a State Tree:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/4fe37838df822fe3ccfe068588e67aa68e851e36.png[/img]


[h3] Detection Meter [/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/81ccbd342b7bbfd72fe35e865db1a9477edebad8.png[/img]

The scheme above is an NPC guard's field of vision in Kvasir, represented by colored zones and associated states:

[b]Alerted State:[/b] Closest to the NPC is a small red zone indicating the "Alerted" state. If the player enters this zone, the NPC becomes immediately aware of the player's presence.

[b]Investigation State:[/b] Beyond the red zone, there is a larger yellow zone that triggers the "Investigation" state when the player enters it. This state is likely less aggressive than the "Alerted" state, suggesting the NPC is suspicious but has not yet confirmed the player's presence.

[b]Investigation Gauge:[/b] At the periphery of the NPC's vision is the green threshold, which is the trigger point for the "Investigation Gauge" to begin filling. This suggests a mechanic where the NPC becomes gradually more suspicious the longer the player stays in this area. The closer the player is to the yellow zone, the faster the Investigation Gauge fills up, increasing the risk of detection.

[b]Visibility Impacts NPC Thresholds:[/b] factors like lighting or the player's stance (standing, sitting, running, etc.) would affect how easily the NPC notices the player.

This is how it ended looking under the hood:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/6e2ae5dd8b05b23c7caf8cc114d13b44967de96d.gif[/img]


Our early mockup of state visualization for enemies (when a certain state is active):
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/4c5c8a2245571251566509b270411ca7b5756dfc.png[/img]

And the in-game implementation. It's pretty cool that we can now play animation on switching states - as in this case the guard let's out a small ghasp.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/8c99f0669f9673abfd184d4682aae287a02396fd.gif[/img]



[h3] Waking up stunned opponents [/h3]

Another thing we did in this iteration is the guards are finally able to wake up each other (placeholder animations).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/b352951758db35d23447d2d223197cf8eae39e3a.gif[/img]

We studied player feedback on MGS and Splinter Cell AI complexity, and we're looking forward to making AIs smarter in how they react to threats, also based on their class in future iterations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/d561431a8344adaead0a34ec22229c19c41b1ec5.png[/img]

That's all for now. Stay tuned for more updates next month!

notes.title: Core Loop: Stealth Meters
notes.content:
KVASIR is heavily inspired by stealth adventure games like Metal Gear Solid and Splinter Cell. And one of the coolest mechanics we noticed there that was so rarely use elsewhere is the "environmental awareness". Meaning how much you blend in and how easy/hard it is to spot you.

Here's an example from Splinter Cell that we used in our documentation:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45289355/e420f9466bdeea047c94dc0c1f3ab3ec34b32714.png[/img]

[h1][b]1. VISIBILITY METER[/b][/h1]

In KVASIR, the visibility meter (aka light indicator) reveals how visible you are in the environment. 

At first it was just how much light are you under right now (hence "light indicator" title). But then we realized that player's visibility should depend not just on the light around you but also on your opponent's sight radius. 

And different opponents will have different sight radius and reaction time. So you'll need to stay in the shadows to outsmart them.

[previewyoutube=OmiRsIRYGug;full][/previewyoutube]

We also have a couple of shorts on the youtube channel, made for the single purpose of adding vids to our steam posts. But turns out Steam doesn't support shorts. So I'll just drop the link to the playlist (but you also can  [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@kvasir_game]follow us onTikTok[/url]):

[previewyoutube=dblQznC-T2o;full][/previewyoutube]

Since we already made the technical component to track visibility, next we'll have to painfully tune it in every single location. 

The challenge here is make the intuitive visibility equal the component's state. E.g. there should be no cases, where the player's sure they are standing in the shadows, but the visibility meter is half-full etc.

[h1][b]2. SOUND METER[/b][/h1]

Just like with light, we also incorporated sound detection. Of course, the opponents will react to sound, so the speed with which you move and the surface matters. 

In our original concept, sound meter shows two values:
[olist]
[*]     player's sound level
[*]     background sound level 
[/olist] Background noise = any noise that is NOT made by the player, having less weight the more distant it is to them.

As long as the player’s sound is not higher than the background - they will not be heard. The rest also depends on opponents hearing radius.

It took us quite some time to figure out how to use the wavy visualizer that we wanted in UE - the one you can see on the vids. So right now it only shows how much sound the player makes. And based on our playtests we'll see if we even need the added complexity of background sound level.

That's all for now. 
You can [url=https://ko-fi.com/projectkvasir]support us on ko-fi[/url] and make the release date a bit closer.

Your balkan dad wishes you a good weekend!

notes.title: Hello there!
notes.content:
[h1] 🌟 How it started >> How it's going 🌟[/h1] 

It’s been less than a month since we launched our Steam page, and we’re absolutely overwhelmed by your warm support and encouragement. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts for checking out our game! 💖

A quick introduction for those new to our journey: about a year ago, [b]Kvasir [/b]began as a passion project of a husband-and-wife duo—[b]Alina[/b] and [b]Arvy[/b]. Together, we’ve spent over a decade each in the game industry—Arvy as a UI/UX lead and artist, and Alina as a producer and narrative designer. 

Being long-time fans of the stealth and immersive sim genres, we’ve felt these areas have been not only  lacking fresh ideas and new titles, but even not repeating what was already achieved in stealth. 

So we decided to take matters into our own hands and make the kind of game we’ve always wanted to play.

However, as two non-coders, diving into Unity and Unreal Engine was a steep uphill battle! Luckily, an old friend and former colleague, [b]Dima[/b], joined our team as the[i] only[/i] person who knows how to wrangle game engines. 

Since then, the journey has been nothing short of turbulent.

Soon all three of us had to find new jobs (only one of us is full-time employed right now) and face financial challenges. 

At one point, we spent months customizing a pre-made solution for the game only to realize it wouldn’t work. Reverting those changes and essentially restarting in October ’24 was a tough pill to swallow, but we’ve come back even more determined.

Through all the ups and downs, we’ve managed to make steady progress, and we’re excited to give you a sneak peek into what we’ve been working on.

Thank you for being a part of this journey. Your support means everything to us as we continue to pour our hearts into Kvasir. 

Stay tuned for more updates! 🙌

🖤 Alina, Arvy, and Dima
